literal_meaning: কানাই গ্রামের ভাগনে (nephew from Kanai village)
figurative_meaning_en: A person of lecherous or immoral character
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে তো কানায়ে ভাগনার মতো, কোথাও শান্তি নেই।
গ্রামে সবাই তাকে কানায়ে ভাগনা বলে ডাকে তার চরিত্রের জন্য।
example_sentences_in_english: He's just like the Kanai nephew, always up to no good with women.
Everyone in the village calls him the Kanai nephew because of his immoral ways.
history: This idiom draws from Bengali folk tales featuring a mischievous nephew named Kanai from a village called Kanai, symbolizing unrestrained and lecherous behavior in rural storytelling traditions.
note: The idiom is rooted in oral folklore and used to describe morally loose individuals in a derogatory manner.
